zh.q: 一条河从山里流到海，一路上留下了什么？
zh.concl: 河流是塑造地表形态的重要外力：它一路侵蚀、搬运、堆积，把河谷加深、拓宽、延长，还在山前、中下游、河口造出三种冲积平原。
points: 整块沙盘是一条 40 km 长的河，从山地一直流到海。
四个部位从上游到下游排开：山区河谷 → 山前冲积扇 → 曲流与河漫滩 → 河口三角洲。
村镇都落在冲积平原上、洪水淹不到的地方（教材 p.37）。

zh.q: 为什么山里的河谷又深又窄，还是个 V 形？
zh.concl: 幼年期落差大、流速快、能量集中，侵蚀以向下和向源头为主，河谷不断加深、延长，所以深而窄、谷壁陡峭、横剖面呈 V 形（切块上谷头随阶段向上游后退，就是溯源侵蚀）。
points: 幼年期河道纵剖面最陡，河床落差 145 m（示意）。
流速 3.38 m/s 时能搬动 152.0 mm 的卵石——水流是有力的。
「能搬动多大的颗粒」比单看流速更直观地说明搬运能力。

zh.q: 河谷后来怎样变宽变浅？
zh.concl: 落差减小以后，向下侵蚀减弱、向两岸侵蚀加强，河谷不断拓宽；经漫长过程，横剖面变成宽而浅的槽形。
points: 宽深比是「谷宽 ÷ 谷深」：10 是 V 形谷，200 是宽而浅的槽形。
剖面里能看到谷壁由陡变缓、谷底由窄槽变成宽平底；灰色虚线是其余阶段的轮廓，可直接对比。
剖面同时露出地层，说明河谷是「切」进原来地面的。

zh.q: 水一出山，为什么先把大石头放下？
zh.concl: 河流流出山区进入平原，地势趋于平缓、河道开阔、流速减慢，搬运的物质逐渐在山前沉积成扇状；几条河流的冲积扇扩大并联，就成为广阔的山前冲积平原。
points: 判据是「本段搬得动的最大粒径明显小于上游」——上游送来的粗颗粒在这里搬不动了。
扇顶（63.3 mm）比扇缘（25.7 mm）粗，说明粗颗粒先落地。
冲积扇是扇状堆积体，不是河谷。

zh.q: 河道弯了以后，冲和淤各在哪一岸？
zh.concl: 河道弯曲后，凹岸（弯道外侧）水流快、受冲刷侵蚀、岸线后退；凸岸（弯道内侧）水流慢、泥沙堆积、岸线前伸；河道因此更弯、河谷更宽。
points: 凹岸是弯道外侧，凸岸是弯道内侧，不是「左岸右岸」。
两岸流速差 1.09 : 0.57 就是冲淤差异的来源。
长江镇江段南岸是凸岸（堆）、北岸是凹岸（冲），所以岸线向北推移。

zh.q: 洪水退去以后，河边留下什么？
zh.concl: 凸岸堆积成水下堆积体，升高扩大后在枯水季节露出水面成为河漫滩；洪水季节被淹没继续接受堆积；多个废弃河漫滩连起来就是宽广的河漫滩平原。
points: 河漫滩是「凸岸堆积体露出水面」的结果，不是流水冲出来的。
汛期来水量 × 1.8，流速 1.05 m/s、能搬动 11.9 mm，比平水期强，但河漫滩仍以堆积为主。
河漫滩平原是冲积平原的主体，沿河呈带状分布。

zh.q: 河口为什么会长出一块三角洲？
zh.concl: 挟带泥沙的河流进入海洋时，入海处水下坡度平缓、流速减慢，泥沙在河口前方沉积成近似三角形的堆积体；随沉积物增加，向海洋一侧扩展，成为三角洲平原。
points: 三角洲的条件是「入海处水下坡度平缓」加「流速减慢」，不是「泥沙多」就够。
河口只搬得动 1.6 mm 的砂，粗颗粒早在中上游卸完了。
前缘 1.8 → 3.6 km，是可以量的「向海扩展」。

zh.q: 汛期里怎样让曲流段搬不动 10 mm 的砾石？
zh.concl: 同一河段能搬动的最大粒径只由流速决定：纵剖面变缓、来水量变小，都会让它降下来。
points: 汛期把来水量抬到 1.8 倍，搬运能力跟着涨。
老年期纵剖面最平缓（落差 51 m），同一河段的流速与搬运能力都最弱。
调小来水量是另一条同样成立的路——两条都指向「流速减慢 → 搬运能力减弱」。

en.q: A river runs from the mountains to the sea. What does it leave along the way?
en.concl: Rivers are an important external force shaping the land surface: along their course they erode, transport and deposit, deepening, widening and lengthening valleys, and building three kinds of alluvial plain at the mountain front, in the middle and lower reaches, and at the mouth.
points: The whole sand table is a 40 km river running from the mountains to the sea.
Four sections line up from upstream to downstream: mountain valley → piedmont alluvial fan → meanders and floodplain → river-mouth delta.
The towns all sit on alluvial plains, where floods don't reach (textbook p. 37).

en.q: Why are mountain valleys deep, narrow and V-shaped?
en.concl: In youth the gradient is steep, the flow fast and the energy concentrated; erosion is mainly downward and headward, so the valley keeps deepening and lengthening, making it deep and narrow with steep walls and a V-shaped cross-section (on the block the valley head retreats upstream with each stage: that is headward erosion).
points: In youth the long profile is steepest, with a channel drop of 145 m (illustrative).
At 3.38 m/s the flow can move 152.0 mm pebbles: the water is powerful.
"How big a grain it can move" shows carrying capacity more directly than flow speed alone.

en.q: How does the valley later become wider and shallower?
en.concl: Once the gradient drops, downcutting weakens and lateral erosion strengthens, so the valley keeps widening; over a long time the cross-section becomes a wide, shallow trough.
points: The width-to-depth ratio is "valley width ÷ valley depth": 10 is a V-shaped valley, 200 a wide, shallow trough.
In the profile the valley walls go from steep to gentle and the floor from a narrow slot to a wide flat bottom; the grey dashed lines are the outlines of the other stages for direct comparison.
The profile also exposes the strata, showing the valley was "cut" into the original ground.

en.q: Once the water leaves the mountains, why does it drop the big stones first?
en.concl: When a river leaves the mountains for the plain, the land flattens, the channel opens out and the flow slows; the material it carries gradually settles at the mountain front as a fan; as the fans of several rivers grow and merge they form a broad piedmont alluvial plain.
points: The criterion is "the largest grain this reach can move is clearly smaller than upstream": the coarse grains brought from upstream can't be carried further here.
The fan apex (63.3 mm) is coarser than the fan edge (25.7 mm), so coarse grains settle first.
An alluvial fan is a fan-shaped deposit, not a valley.

en.q: Once the channel bends, which bank erodes and which fills?
en.concl: Once the channel bends, the concave bank (outside) has fast flow, is scoured and retreats; the convex bank (inside) has slow flow, collects sediment and builds out; the channel bends more and the valley widens.
points: The concave bank is the outside of the bend and the convex bank the inside; not "left bank, right bank".
The flow difference of 1.09 : 0.57 between the banks is the source of the different erosion and deposition.
At Zhenjiang the south bank of the Yangtze is convex (deposits) and the north bank concave (erodes), so the bank moves north.

en.q: What is left by the river after a flood recedes?
en.concl: The convex bank builds an underwater deposit; as it rises and grows it shows above the water at low water as a floodplain; in floods it is submerged and receives more sediment; many abandoned floodplains joined together make a broad floodplain plain.
points: A floodplain is "a convex-bank deposit exposed above the water", not something washed out by flowing water.
In the flood season inflow is × 1.8, flow 1.05 m/s and it can move 11.9 mm, stronger than at normal water, but the floodplain is still mainly depositing.
Floodplains make up most of the alluvial plain and lie in bands along the river.

en.q: Why does a delta grow at the river mouth?
en.concl: When a sediment-laden river enters the sea, the underwater slope is gentle and the flow slows, so the sediment settles in front of the mouth as a roughly triangular deposit; as sediment builds up it spreads seaward and becomes a delta plain.
points: A delta needs "a gentle underwater slope where it enters the sea" plus "slower flow"; "lots of sediment" alone is not enough.
At the mouth it can only move 1.6 mm sand; the coarse grains were dropped long before in the middle and upper reaches.
Front 1.8 → 3.6 km is a measurable "spread toward the sea".

en.q: In the flood season, how do you make the meander reach unable to move 10 mm gravel?
en.concl: The largest grain a reach can move depends only on the flow speed: a gentler long profile or a smaller inflow both bring it down.
points: The flood season raises the inflow to 1.8 times, and carrying capacity rises with it.
In old age the long profile is gentlest (drop 51 m), so the same reach has the weakest flow and carrying capacity.
Reducing the inflow is another equally valid route; both lead to "slower flow → lower carrying capacity".
